archetype: Mardu Vampire typal go-wide linear aggro that kills by trigger rather than by combat: Edgar's eminence mints a body for every Vampire cast from the command zone, three token doublers multiply that body, and three each-opponent damage payoffs (Purphoros, Impact Tremors, Warleader's Call) convert every entry into damage at all three seats. Combat is the second kill, the lords and Shared Animosity its multiplier; two checker-passed lifegain/lifeloss infinites (Bloodthirsty Conqueror plus Vito or Sanguine Bond, verified stacks 004 and 006) are a third route that assembles in one game in twenty and is priced accordingly.

role_assignment.default_role: Beatdown, and now unambiguously so — the deck does not own the long game and should stop pretending it might. strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock names the sources of inevitability as superior late-game card quality, an engine that scales, an unanswerable finisher, or more answers than the table has threats; the only unanswerable finisher here is the Conqueror pairing, and goldfish measures it drawn in 4.8% of games (2.6% by turn six; 24.0% / 14.2% counting the three unrestricted tutors as wildcards). A finisher that shows up one game in twenty is not ownership of the long game, so per strategy:whos-the-beatdown the deck that loses the long game must be the beatdown. What makes the racing plan survive strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry's ~120-life objection is that the payoffs are each-opponent drains rather than combat damage: TOKEN -> DAMAGE is drawn in 43.2% of games at a mean turn of 3.45, and a damage trigger on a token entry hits all three seats at once. Role stays seat-relative (strategy:multiplayer.pod-management): a wide board of first-strike, deathtouch and lifelink bodies plays defence against one opponent while the entry triggers race the other two.
role_assignment.pivot_trigger: Three named events, in the order they usually arrive. (1) A token->damage payoff resolves onto a board that already has a multiplier — the GO-WIDE KILL target, 33.4% assembled, mean turn 4.66 — because from that point each cheap Vampire cast is a burn spell aimed at the table rather than a body waiting on a combat step (strategy:life-as-resource.philosophy-of-fire prices the deck's cards in damage; here the rate is set by how many doublers are down, not by how many creatures survive). (2) Edgar resolving, median turn 6, 52.2% by turn six: he adds first strike, haste and a +1/+1 counter on every Vampire at declare, which is the alpha-strike window. (3) Bloodthirsty Conqueror landing while Vito or Sanguine Bond is already on the battlefield — deploy the second half only into the window strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window describes, since both halves of every surviving pairing include a creature and instant-speed creature removal breaks the loop at any iteration's priority window (stack 006 says so explicitly). Sequence the scariest piece last (strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection): the enchantment payoffs read as durdle, the 5/5 flying deathtouch Vampire does not.

engines.piece: Edgar Markov (eminence) + Anointed Procession + Mondrak, Glory Dominus + Elspeth, Storm Slayer
engines.engine: The ignition, and the one component that never fails to assemble: eminence works from the command zone, so every Vampire spell cast makes a token from turn one whether or not Edgar is castable. Three replacement-effect doublers multiply that token event; stack 002 verifies the doubling is one event, order-independent, and that eminence does not re-trigger on the tokens themselves (created, not cast).
engines.evidence: verified stack 002 (checker pass — 1->2->4 through two doublers); deck-facts roles doubler:tokens 3; goldfish 'A token multiplier or extra token-maker drawn' 79.0% assembled, mean turn 2.68; mean_bodies_by_turn 1.75 at t3, 4.12 at t6, 6.52 at t10

engines.piece: Purphoros, God of the Forge + Impact Tremors + Warleader's Call
engines.engine: The conversion layer, and the deck's answer to the 1-to-3 problem: each creature entering deals damage to EACH opponent, so board width is spent on all three seats simultaneously and never has to survive to a combat step. Stack 008 verifies the leverage at its measured ceiling — four token entries plus the spell's own body is five Purphoros triggers, 10 damage to each opponent from one two-mana Vampire. All three payoffs are enchantments (Purphoros is an indestructible enchantment while devotion to red is under five), which is why this layer is the part of the deck a creature sweeper cannot touch.
engines.evidence: verified stack 008 (checker pass); oracle text (Impact Tremors, Warleader's Call, Purphoros); goldfish 'TOKEN -> DAMAGE drawn' 43.2% assembled / 34.1% by t6, and 'THE GO-WIDE KILL: a token->damage payoff AND a multiplier' 33.4% / 22.5% by t6

engines.piece: The lord package: Legion Lieutenant, Stromkirk Captain, Captivating Vampire, Vampire Socialite, Drana, Cordial Vampire, Patchwork Banner, Shared Animosity, Abzan Falconer
engines.engine: The combat kill. Lords are multiplicative against a token board in a way anthems are not against a fair one — every +1/+1 is paid nine or ten times over. Shared Animosity is the sharpest version (each attacker gets +1/+0 for every other attacking creature sharing a type), and Edgar's attack trigger puts a counter on each Vampire at declare, which Vampire Socialite compounds and Abzan Falconer converts into evasion for everything carrying a counter.
engines.evidence: oracle text (all nine); deck-facts roles buff:counters 10, buff:pump 9, payoff:typal 4; goldfish 'A Vampire lord or anthem drawn (the combat plan)' 82.9% assembled, mean turn 2.58 — the deck's best-assembling component

engines.piece: Sanctum Seeker + Bloodletter of Aclazotz + Throne of the God-Pharaoh + Twilight Prophet
engines.engine: The attack-and-tap drain: Sanctum Seeker pays per attacking Vampire, Throne per tapped creature at your end step, Bloodletter doubles every opponent's loss during your turn (your gain is never doubled — it replaces only opponents' life loss). Nothing dies and nothing enters a graveyard; this is width converted to each-opponent life loss on a second, independent axis from the entry triggers.
engines.evidence: verified stack 003 (checker pass — seven attackers drain 14 per opponent at declare, before blockers); verified stack 007 (checker pass, PARTIALLY REFUTED as a table-kill: seven tapped creatures drain 14 each at end step, which leaves a 15-life opponent alive at exactly 1 — the honest bound is 14 per opponent, not lethal by default)

engines.piece: Bloodthirsty Conqueror + Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose + Sanguine Bond
engines.engine: The deterministic kill, and a layered one rather than a bolted-on one. Conqueror gains you life whenever an opponent loses life — which every entry trigger, every Sanctum Seeker attack and every Throne end step already causes — and Vito or Sanguine Bond turns that gain back into loss. Both pairings are verified as full table-kills at mana_value_needed 0. Their rent is honest for two of three: Conqueror is a 5/5 flying deathtouch Vampire and Vito a three-mana Vampire body, so each is an eminence trigger and a lord target on the way to being half a kill; Sanguine Bond is a five-mana enchantment with no body, no type and no contribution to width, and it is the one slot the token plan is genuinely paying for.
engines.evidence: verified stacks 004 and 006 (both checker pass — deterministic table-kills, retargetable each iteration, the chain crossing a targeted opponent's death); combo_details via deck-facts: 2 contained lines, both two-card infinites, bracket 3, mana_value_needed 0, popularity 64824 and 54630

engines.piece: Caretaker's Talent + Welcoming Vampire + Preacher of the Schism + Twilight Prophet + Night's Whisper
engines.engine: Refill that scales with the plan instead of competing with it: Caretaker's Talent draws whenever one or more tokens enter (once a turn) and at level two copies a token, Welcoming Vampire draws on small creatures entering, Preacher draws on attack and mints a lifelink Vampire, Twilight Prophet drains and refills on ten permanents. This is why the counted card-advantage axis reads low without the deck being short of cards — the draws are board-gated, and a board is what this deck has.
engines.evidence: oracle text (all five); deck-audit card-advantage 4 copies against a target of >=10, with its own note listing Castle Locthwain, Henrika, Midgar, Minas Tirith, Preacher and Savai Triome as uncounted functions; goldfish 'A draw engine drawn' 60.2% assembled

engines.engine: A tax that makes tokens: every artifact or creature entering untapped under any opponent either comes in tapped or hands you a lifelink Vampire. Against three opponents it is a rate that scales with the table's development rather than yours, and both branches are good for you — the tapped branch is a tempo tax on all three seats, the token branch feeds every entry trigger and every lord.
engines.evidence: oracle text; deck-facts roles threat:tokens 10; goldfish counts it inside the 79.0% multiplier-or-extra-token-maker group

engines.piece: Teferi's Protection + Akroma's Will + Flawless Maneuver + Boros Charm + Deflecting Swat + Swiftfoot Boots
engines.engine: Board-wide insurance sized for a deck whose whole plan is a board. Four of the six protect every permanent at once rather than one creature, which is the correct shape when the thing being answered is a sweeper and not a spot removal spell; Akroma's Will doubles as the alpha-strike enabler (double strike and flying, or indestructible and protection from each colour, or both with a commander out).
engines.evidence: oracle text; deck-audit protection 9 copies; goldfish 'Protection held for the swarm' 68.0% assembled, 56.6% by t6

candidate_missing_lines.title: Three doublers stacked: does one eminence trigger make eight bodies?
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Stack 002 verifies 1->2->4 through two replacement effects and that the order of application is immaterial. All three doublers are in the 99 and each reads 'twice that many of those tokens are created instead', so a third application should read 1->2->4->8 as one entry event. The arithmetic is an extrapolation of a verified line, not the verified line itself.

candidate_missing_lines.title: The full conversion rate: one Vampire cast through three doublers into all three entry-damage payoffs
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Stack 008 verifies four token entries plus the cast body as five Purphoros triggers at 2 damage each. Impact Tremors and Warleader's Call carry the same 'whenever a creature you control enters' condition at 1 damage each to each opponent, so the same five entries should read 5 x (2+1+1) = 20 to each opponent. Composition of three separate trigger sources across one entry event is exactly the kind of arithmetic the checker has bounded before (stack 007).

candidate_missing_lines.title: Bloodletter doubling the entry triggers, not just the attack
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Stack 007 verifies Bloodletter doubling each opponent's loss from Throne of the God-Pharaoh during your turn. The entry-damage payoffs cause opponents to lose life during your turn by the same route (damage causes loss of life), so a token wave cast on your own turn should be doubled at every seat. Verified for one loss source, unverified for these three.

candidate_missing_lines.title: A token entry as loop ignition for the surviving infinites
cards: Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Stacks 004 and 006 verify the loop from a stated life-loss seed. Impact Tremors on a token entry IS a life-loss event at every seat, which should feed Conqueror's 'whenever an opponent loses life, you gain that much life' and start the same chain with no combat and no death. The loop is verified; this specific ignition source is not, and the multi-opponent seeding (three simultaneous losses, three Conqueror triggers) is the part that needs resolving.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Abzan Falconer turning Edgar's attack trigger into evasion for the whole swarm
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Edgar's trigger puts a +1/+1 counter on each Vampire you control when he attacks, and Falconer grants flying to each creature you control with a counter on it. If the counters land during the declare-attackers step, the whole attacking board should have flying before blockers are declared — which would make an alpha strike unblockable by a ground board. The timing of the counters relative to the declare-blockers step is the whole question.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Legion's Landing flipping off the swarm and becoming a repeatable token land
cards: Legion's Landing // Adanto, the First Fort
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Legion's Landing transforms when you attack with three or more creatures — a board this deck reaches at a measured 4.12 bodies by turn six — and the back face is a land that makes a lifelink Vampire for {2}{W}, doubled by any doubler in play. The transform condition and the interaction between a token-making land activation and the entry-damage triggers are unresolved here.

matchup_frames.vs_sweeper_control: The trap the go-wide label implies does not fully apply, and the reason is structural: the machine is not made of creatures. Anointed Procession, Impact Tremors, Warleader's Call, Caretaker's Talent, Patchwork Banner, Legion's Landing, Elspeth and an indestructible-and-usually-noncreature Purphoros all survive a creature wrath, and eminence rebuilds from the command zone with no recast tax and no card spent. strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math says assume the wrath over four players, deploy in waves, and buy resilience rather than restraint — this deck's resilience is bought at the permanent layer rather than the body layer, so the correct posture is to commit exactly the width that wins now and keep the next multiplier in hand, not to hold bodies back. Rebuild worst-first. Four board-wide protection instants (68.0% held) mean the pivot turn can be insured, and Teferi's Protection answers the wrath and the counterattack together. The real exposure is a sweeper that hits enchantments — strategy:threat-assessment.answer-economy's held-answers-rot warning applies to the five noncreature answers in the deck: spend one on the enchantment removal you see coming.
matchup_frames.vs_stax: Structurally the deck's best matchup and the pilot should know it. strategy:threat-assessment.resource-denial says taxes attack velocity math directly and that you rarely own the long game under an assembling lock, so you are the beatdown racing the lock's completion. Eminence is the exception a tax cannot reach: it is a triggered ability from the command zone, not a cast, so every Vampire spell still pays double under a Sphere. The curve cooperates — 9 one-drops and 17 two-drops out of 63 spells — while Edgar himself at six mana is the first thing a tax prices out, and the deck does not need him on the battlefield to function. Name your outs early: the piece that beats you is the one that stops tokens entering or taxes creature spells, not the flashiest lock piece.
matchup_frames.vs_aggro: Re-ask the role (strategy:whos-the-beatdown): against a faster deck you are the control, and this deck can take that seat without changing plans. Twenty-nine bodies, lifelink tokens from Legion's Landing and Charismatic Conqueror, first strike from Edgar and Cemetery Gatekeeper, deathtouch from Preacher and Vampire of the Dire Moon, and a 5/5 flying deathtouch Conqueror make a board that blanks an attack step — strategy:card-advantage.virtual's point exactly, that a wide board turns their small creatures into dead cards without drawing anything. Charismatic Conqueror taxes their development on the way in. Spend life freely above the threshold where it buys tempo (strategy:life-as-resource) — the manabase asks for it, with Ancient Tomb, Mana Confluence, Caves of Koilos and four fetches all charging life — but track each opponent's clock separately, because 40 life attacked from three directions is not 40 life.
matchup_frames.vs_combo: You are the clock, and the deck is fast enough to be one: TOKEN -> DAMAGE at a mean turn of 3.45 and a lord package at 2.58 mean the pressure is real before most combo decks are assembled. strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window's standard cuts both ways — the table applies 'does this card win if it resolves' to your presentation too, so count open mana before committing and prefer the win attempt that leaves a rebuilt position if it fails. Here the entry-damage plan is the one that does: a countered or removed multiplier costs a card, an interrupted alpha strike costs a board. The twelve interaction copies over an aggro template's 5-6 are defensible against combo specifically (strategy:threat-assessment.answer-economy: the bar is 'ends the game or ends my deck's function'), but strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry's rule still binds — hold the one-for-ones until the threat is pointed at you, or you are paying a card to protect two bystanders.

distribution_notes: Copies, not entries: 100 copies across 97 entries; 37 land copies in 34 entries, 63 spells. Curve (nonland) 9 / 17 / 19 / 12 / 5 / 1 across mana values 1-6, modal 3 — one step above the format's modal 2 that strategy:deckbuilding.curve reports from EDHREC data, and worth watching in a deck whose plan wants two spells a turn. Roles: 29 threat:body, 10 threat:tokens, 3 doubler:tokens, 10 buff:counters, 9 buff:pump, 7 wincon:drain, 4 wincon:combat, taxonomy coverage 100% with no unclassified cards. deck-audit puts creatures (29) inside the 26-32 aggro band and threat-density at 11 against a floor of 3, consistency 0.921, interaction breadth 5 classes, bracket floor 4. Three axes read under target and one reading is softer than its number: ramp 7 against 10-12 and colour-sources -11 on the worst colour are real, while card-advantage 4 against >=10 is a floor the audit itself qualifies — six further draw functions sit on cards the taxonomy classifies elsewhere. Two axes read over: interaction 12 against an aggro target of 5-6 (six slots the width plan is not getting, and strategy:critical-mass is blunt that a linear deck's defence is speed, redundancy and resilience rather than answers) and protection 9 against 5-7, which is the defensible over-count since four of the nine are board-wide. Mana: black carries 39 of 73 pips across 29 cards against 22 land sources and a 36-source yardstick — strategy:deckbuilding.mana-base.color-sources reads those as a budget and this budget is overdrawn in the colour the deck most needs on turn two. Sixteen lands enter tapped by the count, but only three unconditionally; deck-facts reports no restricted mana. Land drops hit 99.8% on turn two and 92.1% on turn three, first sevens keep at 81.7%, mean mulligans 0.21. Two declared engine components rest on a single card (the surviving infinite's Conqueror half, and Cemetery Gatekeeper as the noncreature answer) — a named card is 7.1% of an opening seven per strategy:deckbuilding.redundancy-vs-tutors, which is the ceiling on those lines rather than a defect in the simulation.
overall_assessment: This is a linear critical-mass deck (strategy:critical-mass) whose threshold is a number of bodies, and whose defining property is that it no longer needs those bodies to survive a combat step. Edgar's eminence is an ignition that assembles 100% of games from the command zone; three replacement-effect doublers make each ignition multiplicative; and three enchantment-based payoffs turn every resulting entry into damage at all three seats. That last layer is the whole answer to strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry's charge against aggro — incremental combat damage cannot get through ~120 life behind three defences, but 'each opponent loses life' scales with the width the engine was already producing, and it is measured drawn in 43.2% of games at a mean turn of 3.45 with a multiplier alongside it in 33.4%. Default role is therefore beatdown (strategy:whos-the-beatdown), and the honest reason is arithmetic rather than temperament: strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock's test for inevitability is an unanswerable finisher or an engine that scales past the table, and the surviving deterministic kill is drawn in 4.8% of games naturally, 24.0% with the three tutors modelled as wildcards. Keeping Bloodthirsty Conqueror, Vito and Sanguine Bond is the right call on strategy:deckbuilding.threat-density's own terms, and specifically on its layering clause rather than its finisher count: Conqueror's trigger condition is fed by every entry-damage trigger, every Sanctum Seeker attack and every Throne end step the deck was already producing, so the pieces overlap the primary plan instead of forming an unconnected second one. What it buys is the deck's only two deterministic table-kills (verified stacks 004 and 006, both at mana_value_needed 0) plus a 5/5 flying deathtouch Vampire and a three-mana Vampire body that pay rent as eminence triggers and lord targets on turns the loop never happens. What it costs is narrower than it looks and should be named exactly: it is not the bracket, since four Game Changers force floor 4 independently of any combo driver; it is one slot — Sanguine Bond, five mana, no body, no creature type, and no contribution to width until a lifegain source is already down. The deck this makes is an aggro deck holding a lottery ticket, not a combo deck holding a fair backup, and that ordering should govern every sequencing decision: race with the tokens, present the loop only in a window strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window would sanction, and never hold back the board to protect a pairing that shows up one game in twenty. The live tension is where the deck's own numbers point rather than where its label does — twelve interaction copies against a linear archetype's five or six, black overdrawn by eleven sources, and a modal mana value that has drifted one step above the format's.
gaps: No section on go-wide / token strategy as such: the best-matching query returns strategy:multiplayer.pod-management at 0.186. The doc has nothing on token doubling as a multiplicative (rather than additive) resource, on why replacement-effect doublers compound while anthems add, or on the ordering rule that makes several doublers order-independent. This deck's entire plan is that arithmetic.

No section on converting board width into non-combat damage. 'Each creature entering deals damage to each opponent' is the single most important effect class in this deck and the corpus can only reach it through strategy:life-as-resource.philosophy-of-fire, which is a burn-deck frame about cards-as-damage, and strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry, which names each-opponent drains in one clause without pricing them. A section on trigger-based kills versus combat kills — sweeper exposure, evasion irrelevance, the fact that the payoff is a noncreature permanent — would be load-bearing for every token deck.

No section on typal / tribal critical mass. Best query score 0.229. Lords are multiplicative against a wide board and additive against a fair one; typal cost reduction (Herald's Horn, Patchwork Banner) is a rebate on nearly every cast; a creature-type commitment narrows the card pool in exchange for a scaling rate. strategy:critical-mass covers linear decks generally but nothing about the typal case specifically.

No treatment of the combo piece that pays rent. strategy:deckbuilding.threat-density has Eisenherz's layering clause and a two-combos rule, both framed for cEDH; there is no guidance on the common Commander decision this deck faces — when a combo half is also a fine fair card (a 5/5 flier, a three-mana lord target), how should its slot be priced against a plan it does not otherwise serve?

Nothing on rebuilding after a sweeper when the engine is noncreature. strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math's advice is about sizing commitment and rebuild packages made of cards in hand; it has no frame for a deck whose engine survives the wrath and whose rebuild is a free trigger from the command zone. The correct commitment level is different when the machine outlives the board.

No section on activated-ability and trigger timing inside combat — specifically when +1/+1 counters or granted abilities from a declare-attackers trigger are visible to a static ability before the declare-blockers step. Two candidate lines here turn on it.
